summary.headline: Anlon Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 102.3% YoY to INR105.61 crore, with EBITDA margin recovering to 23.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR105.61 crore, up 102.3% YoY, and H1 FY27 revenue of INR193.17 crore already exceeds full-year FY26 revenue. EBITDA margin recovered to 23.9% in Q2 from 17.8% in Q1, which management attributes mainly to passing raw material costs on to customers through price revisions. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR380-400 crore and gave FY28 guidance of INR650-700 crore, excluding medical devices and CDMO upside. Operating cash outflow narrowed to INR7.94 crore in H1 FY27 from INR79.44 crore for all of FY26, and the company is targeting positive operating cash flow by end-FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Over 600 bps QoQ recovery from 17.8% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash used in operating activities (H1 FY27)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR79.44 crore for full FY26

segments.name: Anlon Healthcare (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 44.6% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; within it, intermediates were 81.1% and API 17.1%, with the balance nutraceuticals and other products. Standalone utilisation is 85-86%.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics
segments.commentary: Contributed 43.7% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; has opened an industrial and fine chemicals vertical as a new revenue stream outside pharma. Management cites a sustainable EBITDA margin of 20-23% and PAT margin of 11-13%.

segments.name: Bizotic Lifescience
segments.commentary: Contributed 11.7% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; provides ready-to-operate API capacity at a second manufacturing site. Share swap to take the company to 100% ownership was said to be completing within 8-10 days.

segments.name: Anlon Medicos (formulations, formerly Remember India)
segments.commentary: Entered finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules) with access to over 30 formulation dossiers; operations start from Q3 FY27. Management expects first revenue in Q4 FY27 and sees a tablet/capsule peak of INR80-90 crore.

segments.name: Anlon Biologics and Anlon Medico (new subsidiaries)
segments.commentary: Both incorporated in the period. Anlon Biologics targets peptides, oligonucleotides and biosimilars, with first revenue in Q4 FY28; Anlon Medico targets surgical implants and devices, with first revenue from Q3 FY28 and INR70-80 crore expected within 3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR380-400 crore; management said it is almost in line with that target.
FY28 revenue guidance of INR650-700 crore (INR680-700 crore in a later answer), excluding medical devices and CDMO upside.
Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 25-28%; current run-rate is 23-24%. Management said FY27 full-year margin could reach 25-26%, and FY28 is 'very early to commit'.
Long-run consolidated sustainable EBITDA margin of 23-25% and PAT margin of 11-13%, per management's segment-weighted view.
Positive operating cash flow targeted by end-FY27. Working capital cycle nominal target of 170-180 days; receivable days are being cut to 90-100 from 130-140.
Dividend decision deferred; management will review cash availability and free cash flow around Q4 FY27 results.
Capital raise of up to INR250 crore being finalised by end-November, subject to AGM approval; INR65-70 crore term loan planned for capex.
capex_capacity: Group installed capacity is about 1,900-2,000 MTPA against 400 MTPA at the Anlon parent facility; consolidated utilisation is 65-67%, expected to stay flat for the next two quarters.

Rajkot greenfield expansion adds about 1,200 MTPA via 8 new clean lines, targeted for Q1 FY28 (construction on track; a public hearing in December could cause a 1-2 month delay). Expansion of 500 MTPA planned across the group; Apiqo's 500-600 MTPA expansion is also due by Q1 FY28.
Of the INR130 crore expansion capex, only INR15-20 crore has been spent so far; maximum spend expected by December as advances are paid to suppliers.
Anlon Medicos injectable facility expansion has started, with injectables expected by end-FY28.
CDMO: 3 molecules for 2 global innovators; first molecule commercial supply slipped to end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27 from Q3 FY27. Other two in validation with commercialisation after H1 FY28 (6-8 months).
demand_pricing: Price revisions passed through to customers were the main driver of margin recovery; raw material prices are not normalised and remain near post-March war levels.
Standalone API vs intermediate mix is about 20:80 by revenue; management says API and intermediate both run at about 35% gross margin.

Portfolio is 21 DMFs filed; 4 products already commercialised and validated among the 7 targeted for FY27. 3 filings planned by December and the rest by February-March; one filing may slip 1-2 months.
Ketoprofen US DMF is on hold pending a US FDA trigger from a customer; no plan to file directly for the US.
Management claims cost is 10% or more below Chinese prices for its key molecules and that it has displaced Chinese suppliers in Europe, LATAM, Japan and Korea.
Loxoprofen topical gel for India: CDSCO/DCGI approval expected by at least Q1 FY28; management says revenue could be 2-3x the tablet/capsule level once launched pan-India.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR400 crore, and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance remains INR380-400 crore, almost on track. FY28 is guided at INR650-700 crore, based on existing projects and the expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay within 25-30% and when does Anlon Medicos start revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current run-rate is 23-24%, with a sustainable 25-27% targeted; FY28 is early to commit. Anlon Medicos first revenue was pushed to Q4 FY27 because of re-registration and takeover approval delays.

qa_highlights.question: Has the CDMO commercial supply started?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet; the first molecule commercial supply is delayed 1-2 months to end-Q3 or early Q4 FY27. Molecules 2 and 3 are validated but commercialisation will take 6-8 months, after H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise 600 bps QoQ, and what is the working capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly price pass-through to customers, as raw materials have not normalised. Nominal working capital cycle is 170-180 days; receivable collection is improved to 90-100 days from 130-140 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and what is the medical device contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated utilisation is 65-67%; standalone is 85-86%. Medical devices are excluded from FY28 projections and are expected to reach INR70-80 crore in 3 years at EBITDA above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of the capital raise and how is capex funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Up to INR250 crore is being finalised for capex in parent and subsidiaries, including Anlon Biologics. Separately, INR65-70 crore term loan is planned, with the balance from internal accruals.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on continued price pass-through, and raw material costs remain elevated; sustainable margin is still below the 25-28% target.
Capacity expansion timing: Rajkot's 1,200 MTPA line and Apiqo's expansion are targeted for Q1 FY28 but depend on a December public hearing and regulatory approvals.
Working capital remains stretched: receivable days about 123 (annualised) and payable days about 40; debt has risen, and management did not give a deadline for the INR65-70 crore term loan.
CDMO and Anlon Medicos revenue timing has slipped repeatedly; the first CDMO commercial supply is now expected late in Q3 or early Q4 FY27.
Governance and disclosure: an analyst questioned audit coverage across subsidiaries, and management's answer was that consolidated numbers were also reviewed, which needs verification.
Dividend intent is undecided, and the INR250 crore fundraise details are not finalised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and Q2 margin recovery, but cautious and hedged on forward margins, CDMO timing and FY28 specifics. Management repeatedly says it is 'very early to commit' and gave a few inconsistent answers, including the FY28 revenue range and the Anlon Medicos start quarter.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 recovered to 23.9%, an improvement of over 600 basis points sequentially.
Majorly, we have passed on the cost to the customer. Because raw material prices are not normalized yet.

So, we are just focusing on the products where we are strong in terms of the chemistry, where we are strong in handling of the hazardous and poisonous material, which can give us the leverage against the China.
